content:
Ghulam Ali Okarvi was a prominent Islamic scholar and preacher from Pakistan. He was known for his passionate and vocal advocacy of Sunni Islam and his strong opposition to Ahmadiyya, a controversial Islamic sect. Okarvi was a prolific writer and speaker, and his works and speeches were widely respected in the Sunni community.

Okarvi founded the Jamaat Ahle Sunnat organization, which aimed to promote the teachings of Sunni Islam and combat what he viewed as heretical beliefs and practices. He also traveled extensively throughout Pakistan and other countries to preach his message and engage in debates with members of other Islamic sects.

Okarvi's teachings were controversial in some circles, as he was known for his outspoken criticism of certain Islamic groups and individuals. Despite this, he maintained a large following of supporters who admired his commitment to upholding what he believed to be the true teachings of Islam.

Ghulam Ali Okarvi passed away in 1998, but his legacy continues to be remembered and respected by many in the Sunni Muslim community.
